problems: sources_total counts the 14 distinct pages opened; per-dossier source counts (9+8+4) sum to 21 because Sekigahara, Matsumae clan, Azuchi-Momoyama, Sengoku, Ikko-ikki and Kaga Province are cited in more than one dossier. Tokugawa used five pages of its own (Tokugawa shogunate, Invasion of Ryukyu, Matsumae Domain, Kuril Islands dispute, Hakodate bugyo) plus three shared, effectively one over its budget of five; warring-states-japan used exactly nine.

ryukyu-kingdom (jk-01-b) records its 1609 contest, 1609 vassalage and 1611 loss against 'satsuma-domain'; tokugawa-shogunate records the matching events against 'ryukyu-kingdom'. Decide: create satsuma-domain or rename those counterparts in ryukyu-kingdom to tokugawa-shogunate.

Cliopatria's Ryukyu Kingdom row ends in 1520 and the Tokugawa row carried Okinawa from 1600; every Tokugawa keyframe now subtracts Okinawa, so ryukyu-kingdom must supply the island's shape 1521-1879 (its own dossier does this by new keyframes) or Okinawa will be blank.

tokugawa-shogunate ends 3 January 1868 (Cliopatria runs to 1869). The 1869 year for north-eastern Japan and Hokkaido has no state unless empire-of-japan takes all Japan in 1869 or rebel dossiers (Northern Alliance, Republic of Ezo) are written. empire-of-japan should also carry the matching 1868 gain, the 1868 contest end and the 1875 Sakhalin exchange.
joseon (jk-02) should carry the matching occupation events (Japanese occupation 5/1592 to 1/1593 around Busan, Seoul and Pyongyang; 1/1593 to 12/1598 on the southern coast) with roles reversed.

warring-states-japan is a Cliopatria period shape, not a state: the Ashikaga row (jk-01-b) already holds only the Kyoto remnant from 1468, so the two dossiers are mirrored (contest 1467-1477, gain 1468, gain 9/1573); the colour registry gives it the same colour as tokugawa-shogunate.
